correctness.rationale: From a proper seed, every peripheral vertex in a clique of size s<a has degree s<=q-2 and therefore can never acquire q-1 distinctly colored neighbors: it must be seeded. A maximum clique permits at most one blank. If the hub is blank, no peripheral blank is forced first, hence the hub must first see all a noncentral colors. These necessities suffice. Each completed seed has one full proper extension. Counting full colorings gives q(a!)^B U; the hub-covered and hub-blank contributions are z^(m+1)(z+a)^B and z^m(z+a)^B, with the unique globally omitted-color configurations subtracted as aV z^m. H(z)=(z+1)(z+a)^B-c has H prime derivative roots at -a and -(a+B)/(B+1), neither a root of H; sign and monotonicity show one real root if B even and two if B odd, with H(0)=0 solely for G=K_q. The complete graph gives q! z^(q-1)(z+q). Independent brute propagation on seven configurations (a=2 or 3, unequal peripheral orders included) matched every enumerator coefficient; e.g. (2,2) gives {2:24,3:96,4:60,5:12}. All-size proof rests on local argument, not brute enumeration.
